page.overview:
Who is Miles Axlerod?

Miles Axlerod is the main antagonist of Cars 2.

Not much is known about Axlerod's history with the lemons, Axlerod Industries, and Sterling. According to Mel Dorado, he has been known by the world for trying to traveling around without using a GPS and nearly perishes in a rainforest, but emerges more than a month later, using a fuel that is said to be made out of the natural elements. He then reportedly sold off his oil company, converted himself to an electric car, and invents Allinol, an environment-friendly fuel substance. He then created the World Grand Prix as an opportunity to demonstrate the possibility of alternative fuels.

In reality, Axlerod never went through with the electric conversion and continues to control a large number of oil assets, including offshore rigs. Allinol is merely gasoline tainted to violently combust when hit by EMP. He planned to sabotage the World Grand Prix by using concealed EMP weaponry to damage any racers using them, which would discredit alternative fuels entirely, allowing the lemons to profit off their paranoia. Although he maintained his facade well, a few like Sarge are skeptical.

At the opening ceremony in Tokyo, one day before the first race, Axlerod goes on stage to introduce the World Grand Prix racers to the press. While Axlerod is introducing McQueen, Mater suddenly rushes to the fountain behind them, having eaten too much wasabi. Feeling embarrassed, McQueen tries to explain to Axlerod about Mater, but Axlerod seems glad, as he thanks Mater for calling into the Mel Dorado Show. However, Axlerod leaks some oil beneath him and Mater, which it is immediately thought that Mater had leaked oil (being the car equivalent of urinating). While McQueen scolds Mater and orders him to take care of himself, Axlerod gets a member of staff to clean the oil up. Later, Zündapp calls Axlerod to inform him that Redline passed down secret information. The first race starts as usual, but throughout the whole race, three racers get their engines blown, leading the press to believe that Allinol might be the reason why. Axlerod dismisses this to the press, saying that his fuel would have nothing to do with it.
